title: ACCESS-Style Practice Test — Form B
overview: A second full practice test with new topics. Listen, read, write, and speak your best. The questions grow more challenging as each part goes on.

sections.title: Listening
sections.directions: You will hear short talks and conversations read aloud. Listen carefully. After each one, answer the question. Choose the best answer or follow the steps in the question.

items.title: Field Trip Reminder
items.prompt: What should students bring on the field trip?
items.correct: Correct. The teacher reminds students to bring a packed lunch.
items.support: The needed item usually follows the word "bring" or "remember."
items.extension: What time does the bus leave?

teacher.prompt: Why eat lunch outside on the trip?

script: Good morning. Tomorrow is our field trip to the science museum. Remember to bring a packed lunch, because we will eat outside in the park. Wear comfortable shoes for walking.

items.title: Gym Class Instructions
items.prompt: What does the coach tell students to do before running?
items.correct: Correct. The coach says to stretch and warm up first.
items.support: The word "before" tells you the order of actions.

teacher.noTech: Read aloud; thumbs up on the answer.
teacher.prompt: What happens if athletes skip a warm-up?

script: Listen, class. Today we are going to run laps around the track. But before you run, you must stretch and warm up your muscles so you do not get hurt. Take two minutes to stretch now.

items.title: Recipe Ingredients
items.prompt: Which ingredients does the speaker list for the smoothie?
items.correct: Correct. The smoothie needs bananas, milk, and strawberries.
items.hint: Track the list joined by "and." Salt was not mentioned.
items.support: Listen for each item in the list and ignore items that are not said.
items.extension: What would you add to make it your own?

teacher.challenge: Add a distractor and ask why it is wrong.
teacher.prompt: Which item gives the smoothie a sweet taste?

script: Here is how to make a simple smoothie. Into the blender, put two bananas, one cup of milk, and a handful of strawberries. Then blend until smooth.

items.title: Steps of an Experiment
items.prompt: Put the steps of the plant experiment in the order the teacher describes.

items.text: Plant a seed in each cup.
Place one cup in the sun and one in a dark closet.
Record how the plants grow each day.

items.correct: Correct. You followed the order: fill soil, plant seeds, place cups, record growth.
items.hint: Listen for order words: first, next, then, finally.
items.support: Each signal word marks the next step in the experiment.
items.extension: Which cup do you predict will grow taller? Why?

teacher.prompt: Why do scientists keep one plant in the dark?

script: Here is our plant experiment. First, fill two cups with soil. Next, plant one seed in each cup. Then place one cup in the sun and put the other in a dark closet. Finally, record how the plants grow each day in your notebook.

items.title: Comparing Survey Results
items.prompt: Complete the summary of the reading survey.

segments.text: More students chose mystery books, so mystery was
than science fiction. Comic books received the

items.correct: Correct. Mystery was more popular than science fiction, and comics got the fewest votes.
items.hint: Listen for comparison words: more popular, fewest.
items.support: Comparatives compare two; superlatives like "fewest" compare all.
items.extension: How would you display this data in a graph?

teacher.use: Harder item integrating data and comparison.

script: Here are the results of our class reading survey. Mystery books got fourteen votes, science fiction got nine votes, and comic books got only three votes. So mystery was more popular than science fiction, and comic books received the fewest votes. Now complete the summary.

items.title: A Group Decision
items.prompt: What do the students decide to do about the broken supplies?

options.text: Tell the teacher and ask for new ones

items.correct: Correct. They agree to tell the teacher and ask for new supplies.
items.hint: Listen to the END, where they reach a decision.
items.support: The decision in a dialogue usually comes after weighing the options.
items.extension: Why is telling the teacher the responsible choice?

teacher.use: Hardest listening item, inference from dialogue.
teacher.function: Drawing a conclusion from a conversation.
teacher.lower: Read twice; pause at the decision.

script: Listen to two students in the art room. Ana says, "These scissors are broken. Should we just use them anyway?" Jordan says, "No, that could be dangerous. We should tell Ms. Lee and ask for new ones." Ana answers, "You're right. Let's go ask her now."

sections.title: Reading
sections.directions: Read each passage on your own. Then answer the questions about it. You may look back at the passage. Choose the best answer or click the correct sentence.

items.title: Finding a Detail
items.prompt: Click the sentence that tells what penguins use their wings for.
passage: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly through the air like most birds.
Instead, penguins use their strong wings like paddles to swim quickly underwater.
Their smooth feathers keep them warm in the icy ocean.
On land, penguins waddle slowly, but in the water they are fast and graceful.

sentences.text: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly through the air like most birds.
Instead, penguins use their strong wings like paddles to swim quickly underwater.
Their smooth feathers keep them warm in the icy ocean.
On land, penguins waddle slowly, but in the water they are fast and graceful.

items.correct: Correct. Penguins use their wings like paddles to swim.
items.hint: Find the sentence with the word "wings."
items.support: Scan for the key word "wings" and read what they do with them.
items.extension: How do penguins move on land?

teacher.challenge: Find use of wings and feathers.
teacher.prompt: How are penguins different from most birds?

items.title: Vocabulary in Context
items.prompt: Complete the summary using the passage.
passage: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly through the air like most birds.
Instead, penguins use their strong wings like paddles to swim quickly underwater.
Their smooth feathers keep them warm in the icy ocean.
On land, penguins waddle slowly, but in the water they are fast and graceful.

segments.text: keep them warm in the icy ocean.

items.correct: Correct. Penguins cannot fly, and their feathers keep them warm.
items.hint: Reread for what penguins cannot do and what keeps them warm.
items.support: Use the words around each blank to choose the term that fits.
items.extension: What word describes how penguins move on land?

teacher.prompt: How did the passage help you choose feathers?

items.title: Main Idea
items.prompt: Which sentence best states the main idea of the passage?
passage: When people work together, they can solve problems no one could solve alone.
A soccer team wins when players pass the ball and support each other.
Scientists often share data so they can make discoveries faster.
In many situations, cooperation leads to better results than working alone.

options.text: Soccer players pass the ball to win.
Working together often leads to better results than working alone.

items.correct: Correct. The whole passage is about how cooperation leads to better results.
items.hint: The main idea covers the WHOLE passage, not one example.
items.support: The examples about soccer and scientists support one big point.
items.extension: Give another example of teamwork from your own life.
readFor: a detail vs the main idea

teacher.prompt: How do the examples support the main idea?

items.title: Cause and Effect
items.prompt: Click the sentence that explains WHY the city built more bike lanes.
passage: Last year, traffic in the city became very heavy during rush hour.
Many people complained that the roads were crowded and the air was polluted.
Because so many residents wanted cleaner air and shorter trips, the city built more bike lanes.
Now more people ride bikes to work, and the streets are a little less crowded.

sentences.text: Last year, traffic in the city became very heavy during rush hour.
Many people complained that the roads were crowded and the air was polluted.
Because so many residents wanted cleaner air and shorter trips, the city built more bike lanes.
Now more people ride bikes to work, and the streets are a little less crowded.

items.correct: Correct. The city built bike lanes because residents wanted cleaner air and shorter trips.
items.hint: Look for the word "because," which signals a reason.
items.extension: What was the effect of building bike lanes?

teacher.prompt: How did the bike lanes change the city?

items.title: Inference
items.prompt: Which statements can you infer from the passage?
passage: Maya spent three weekends testing which paper towel soaked up the most water.
She recorded her results carefully in a notebook and made a neat bar graph.
On the day of the science fair, her hands shook a little as the judges walked up.
When they smiled and asked thoughtful questions, Maya felt proud of all her hard work.

options.text: Maya worked hard on her project.
Maya was a little nervous at the fair.
Maya did her project in one hour.

items.correct: Correct. The text shows Maya worked hard, felt nervous, and organized her data carefully.
items.hint: One choice is the opposite of the text. She spent three weekends, not one hour.
items.support: An inference is supported by clues, even if not stated directly.
items.extension: What clue shows Maya was nervous?

teacher.use: Inference item with a narrative passage.
teacher.challenge: Cite the clue for each answer.
teacher.prompt: How did the author show Maya's effort?

items.title: Author's Purpose
items.prompt: Why did the author most likely write this passage?
passage: Your body needs water to work properly every single day.
Drinking enough water helps you think clearly and stay full of energy.
If you wait until you feel very thirsty, your body is already low on water.
So keep a water bottle nearby and take small sips throughout the day.

options.text: To tell a funny story about water
To persuade readers to drink enough water
To list the names of rivers

items.correct: Correct. The author gives reasons and advice to persuade readers to drink enough water.
items.hint: Notice the advice at the end. The author wants you to DO something.
items.support: When a text gives reasons and tells you to act, the purpose is to persuade.
items.extension: What advice does the author give at the end?
readFor: what the author wants you to do

teacher.function: Analyzing why a text was written.
teacher.challenge: Compare to the teamwork passage's purpose.
teacher.prompt: How is persuading different from explaining?

sections.title: Writing
sections.directions: Read each task carefully. Plan your ideas, then write a clear response in complete sentences. Use the word bank and sentence frames to help you. Check your work before you finish.

items.title: Describe and Explain
items.prompt: Describe a tool or object you use at school and explain how it helps you. Write 4-6 sentences.
items.correct: Good work. A strong response describes the object clearly and explains how it helps.
items.hint: Name the object, describe it, and explain how it helps you with examples.
items.support: Use the frame "One object I use is ___. It helps me ___ because ___."
items.extension: Explain what would be harder without this object.

teacher.challenge: Add a comparison to another tool.
teacher.prompt: How does this object make your work easier?

items.title: Compare Two Options
items.prompt: Compare doing homework right after school with doing it later in the evening. Which is better and why? Write a paragraph.
items.responsePlaceholder: Both doing homework after school and in the evening ...
items.correct: Good work. A strong response compares both options and reaches a clear conclusion.
items.hint: Show one similarity, two differences, then say which is better and why.
items.support: Use "Both ___" for similarity and "However" for difference, then conclude with "Overall."
items.extension: Explain when your answer might change.

teacher.noTech: Plan with a chart, then write.
teacher.prompt: What helped you decide which option was better?

sections.title: Speaking
sections.directions: You will be given a topic and a short time to plan. Then you will speak your answer aloud in complete sentences. Use the sentence frames to organize your ideas. Speak clearly and stay on topic.

items.title: Explain a Process
items.prompt: Explain how to get ready for a test. Speak 4-5 sentences using order words.
items.correct: Good work. A strong answer uses order words and clear steps.
items.hint: Use a different order word for each step: first, next, then, finally.
items.support: Begin each step with an order word, like "First, you review your notes."
items.extension: Explain what could happen if you skip studying.
items.adminScript: Think about how you get ready for a test. I want you to explain the steps. Speak four or five sentences and use order words like first, next, then, and finally. You have one minute to plan, then you will speak.

teacher.prompt: Which study step helps you most?

items.title: Make and Defend a Recommendation
items.prompt: A new student wants to join a club. Recommend one club and explain why with two reasons. Speak 5-6 sentences.
items.correct: Good work. A strong answer recommends a club and supports it with two clear reasons.
items.hint: Name the club, give two reasons with "because," and end with a conclusion.
items.support: Structure: recommendation, reason one, reason two, conclusion.
items.extension: Mention one reason a different student might choose another club.
items.adminScript: Imagine a new student wants to join a club at your school. I want you to recommend one club and explain why. Speak five or six sentences. Give two reasons using the word because, and finish with a conclusion. You have two minutes to plan, then you will speak.

teacher.use: Final speaking task, recommendation with support.
teacher.challenge: Respond to a peer who prefers a different club.
